textbookText: Equivalent weight of an element can be defined as number of parts by weight of which combines with or replaces 1.008 parts by weight of hydrogen or 8 parts by weight of oxygen or 35.5 parts by weight of chlorine. The equivalent weights of those metals which can replace hydrogen from aqueous mineral acids can be determined by hydrogen displacement method. In other words, equivalent weights of the metals having lower reduction potentials than those of hydrogen can be determined by this method. Therefore, equivalent weight of the metals like Zn, Mg, Fe, Al etc. can be determined by this method.

PROCESS

Take a definite weight of the given metal (about 0.025 — 0.03 gm) and place it in a beaker. Cover it with a short stem funnel. Add water so that the stem of the funnel completely dips under water. Now fill the eudiometer tube half with bench sulphuric acid and half with water.
Close its mouth with thumb (there should not be any air bubbles inside the tube). Invert the eudiometer tube over the stem of the funnel. Clamp the tube with stand.

THEORY

Equivalent weight of an element is defined as the number of parts by weight of which displaces or combines with 1.008 parts by weight of hydrogen or 8 parts by weight of hydrogen or 35.5 parts by weight of chlorine.
The equivalents weight of the metals which can replace hydrogen from aqueous mineral acids (e.g. Zn, Mg, Fe) can be determined by hydrogen displacement method.
MgS04 + H2 t Mg + H2S04 In other words, equivalent weight of the metals having lower reduction potential than that of hydrogen can be found by this method.
In this method, a given piece of metal is treated with dilute H2S04 or dilutes HCl. Then the weight of H2 gas evolved is determined. Finally, weight of metal is calculated by using the relation:
Weight of metal Equivalent weight = Weight of hydrogen X 1.008 Equivalent weight x Weight of hydrogen Weight of metal = 1.008
